govdocs-archive_org--andras-laszlo-berse: László’s god-lore sayings — from the Berserker sheaf — string the Hungarian old-way man’s terse rede. The short saws boil high thought down small. The book is a gem of the old way. Each saw pays thinking on. The sheaf is slim but deep.
govdocs-archive_org-by-rene-guenon-berse: René Guénon’s Veil of Isis — from the Berserker Books archive — gathers the great traditionalist’s essays. The French metaphysician’s pages distill perennial wisdom. Each essay rewards slow reading. His influence runs deep. The book is a gem of traditionalist thought.
govdocs-archive_org-d-herman-wirth-berse: Herman Wirth’s Beginning of Mankind — from the Berserker Books archive — presents the Dutch scholar’s Atlantis theories. The fringe prehistorian’s pages belong to alternative history. Scholars reject his claims. The Nazis once prized his work. The book should be read critically.
govdocs-archive_org-e-bruno-cariou-berse: Bruno Cariou’s Masquerade — from the Berserker Books archive — is a work of traditionalist literature. The file’s pages belong to the archive’s esoteric collection. Its full context is unclear. Archivists value such fragments. The book is a curiosity of the shelves.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JacksonDouglasD: Douglas Jackson’s I Saw the President Assassinated is a witness account. Jackson was a Dallas policeman. His words count. Eyewitnesses shape the case. His account endures. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KennedyBooks_Ke: This item — Kennedy Books, creator unknown — is a file on the JFK literature. The bookshelf grew by the year. Bibliographies guide researchers. The list endures. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
the-three-clerks: Anthony Trollope's Three Clerks — young men in the Civil Service, their loves, debts, and ambitions — shows the novelist's early power. London office life, done with Trollope's sure and sympathetic hand. A delightful early Trollope, full of promise. Charley Tudor's scrapes provide the comedy; Alaric's ambition the warning.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-candles: This 1913 reference piece on altar candlesticks — the holders of the sanctuary lights. Augustin Schulte describes their forms. Brass and silver lift the flames. Their design serves devotion. The altar's golden guard. Their flames guard the tabernacle's door. Their design follows the Roman models.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arawaks: A 1913 entry on the Arawaks — the gentle people of the Caribbean. Adolph Bandelier tells their sad story. Columbus found them on his isles. Disease and slavery swept them away. The first Americans to meet Europe. Their hammocks gave Europe the word.
